subject.title: [Bug]: `openclaw models auth login` on node host writes OAuth token locally instead of syncing to gateway

question: Should remote node-host `openclaw models auth login` fail closed before provider auth starts, or should OpenClaw support a gateway-side credential forwarding flow for this case?
rationale: The choice determines whether a node host may acquire and transfer provider OAuth material for a gateway-owned model runtime, which is both a credential-boundary and product behavior decision.

options.title: Fail closed before auth starts
options.body: Block auth login when node-host config points at a non-loopback gateway and instruct the user to run the command on the gateway host; this is the narrowest safe repair.

options.title: Design gateway credential forwarding
options.body: Add an authenticated gateway-side flow that stores the provider credential in the gateway auth store without first consuming it into the node-local store.

options.title: Warn but allow local write
options.body: Keep local writes possible with an explicit warning, accepting that users can still consume credentials on the wrong host.

recommendation.title: Fail closed before auth starts
recommendation.body: Block auth login when node-host config points at a non-loopback gateway and instruct the user to run the command on the gateway host; this is the narrowest safe repair.

likelyOwner.reason: He authored the maintainer draft for this exact guard and already framed the fail-closed behavior and verification path.
